title: PR Merge Strategies: Merge, Squash & Rebase

options.text: Combines all of the PR's commits into a single commit on the base branch
Creates a merge commit with two parents
Deletes the PR's commits without merging
Replays each commit individually onto the base

questions.explanation: Squash and merge collapses every commit in the PR into one new commit on the base branch, keeping history linear and tidy.

questions.prompt: Which merge method creates a merge commit with two parents?

options.text: None of them create a merge commit

questions.explanation: The 'Create a merge commit' method adds all the branch's commits plus a two-parent merge commit. Squash and rebase both avoid a merge commit.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Rebase and merge produces a linear history without a merge commit
Squash and merge reduces a branch to one commit on the base
A merge commit preserves all the branch's commits and adds a merge commit
Rebase and merge keeps the branch's original commit hashes

questions.explanation: Rebase is linear with no merge commit, squash collapses to one commit, and the merge-commit method keeps everything plus a merge commit. Rebase rewrites commits, so the hashes change.

questions.prompt: The merge method that reduces all of a PR's commits to a single commit is called '______ and merge'.
questions.explanation: Squash and merge combines the PR's commits into one commit on the base branch.

questions.prompt: Your PR has eight noisy 'wip'/'fix' commits, and the team wants main to read as one commit per feature. Which method fits best?

options.text: None — you must clean the commits by hand first

questions.explanation: Squash and merge collapses the eight noisy commits into a single clean commit on main — exactly the one-commit-per-feature history the team wants.

questions.prompt: Match each merge method to its result on the base branch.

pairs.right: All commits plus a two-parent merge commit
Commits replayed linearly, no merge commit

questions.explanation: Merge-commit keeps everything plus a merge commit; squash yields one commit; rebase replays commits with no merge commit; both squash and rebase give linear history.
